approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying Fairmont Public Utilities commercial or industrial electric customer at the installation site.
Select a measure covered by the current 2026 business incentive materials and satisfy its equipment, efficiency, installation, and customer-class specifications.

Submit the applicable application with project scope, equipment information, estimated costs or savings, and other form-specific documentation; obtain advance authorization where the selected form requires it.
Complete the qualifying project within the authorization period and provide final invoices, installation records, and access for any required inspection or verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Fairmont's current 2026 business materials describe prescriptive and custom incentives under objective customer, equipment, documentation, and verification rules rather than competitive scoring. A conforming project is likely to be paid, although the mapped low-flow-fixture measure was not found in the current business list.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Fairmont member page links 2026 business forms for lighting, cooling and heat pumps, refrigeration, food service, energy management, motors, fans, pumps, variable-frequency drives, compressed air, and custom projects. Low-flow fixtures were not listed.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying Fairmont Public Utilities residential electric customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a product or measure appearing in the current residential rebate materials and meet its efficiency, equipment, and installation specifications.
Submit the current rebate application with account information, proof of purchase, model or certification information, and any contractor or installation documentation requested for the measure.
Comply with measure-specific timing, quantity, and verification requirements.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Fairmont currently publishes residential offers for ENERGY STAR products, cooling, electric-vehicle charging, and related efficiency measures, but the accessible official page does not substantiate every mapped category, including the commercial-dishwasher mapping. A qualifying current measure can receive a rebate, but the full legacy opportunity scope is not established.
reviews.evidenceText: Fairmont's current page links 2026 residential rebate summaries and applications for ENERGY STAR products, electric-vehicle chargers, cooling, efficient motors, and air sealing. The page did not expose complete current terms for all mapped measures.

approvalRequirements: Finance an eligible stabilized multifamily property through a Fannie Mae Delegated Underwriting and Servicing lender.
Obtain the required High Performance Building report or equivalent approved assessment identifying eligible energy and water improvements.

Commit to improvements projected to meet the current Green Rewards combined energy-and-water savings threshold, including the required minimum energy-savings component; a low-flow-fixture project alone may not satisfy that threshold.
Pass property, borrower, loan, and project underwriting and establish any required improvement escrow at closing.
Install the committed improvements within the required post-closing period and provide completion, certification, and ongoing utility-performance documentation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Green Rewards is a mortgage-financing product subject to lender and Fannie Mae underwriting, property qualification, savings analysis, and post-closing performance obligations. Water fixtures can be eligible improvements, but the mapped low-flow measure cannot by itself establish the required combined savings profile.
reviews.evidenceText: Fannie Mae's current Green Rewards materials include WaterSense low-flow fixtures as eligible improvements, require a qualifying multifamily loan and building report, impose combined energy-and-water savings commitments, and require timely installation and reporting after closing.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying full-time Hawaii farmer, rancher, or aquacultural operator under the Agricultural Loan Division rules.
Propose an eligible alternative-energy project for the agricultural or aquacultural operation, such as a qualifying photovoltaic system.
Submit the loan application with project scope, vendor or cost information, business and financial records, repayment information, and any requested security or collateral documentation.
Pass project-eligibility and credit underwriting and execute the approved loan and security documents before disbursement.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The Hawaii Department of Agriculture offers current alternative-energy financing, but approval depends on applicant status, project qualification, repayment capacity, security, and loan underwriting. Eligible solar equipment does not create an entitlement to financing.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Agricultural Loan Division page offers alternative-energy loans to qualifying full-time agricultural and aquacultural operators for renewable technologies, including photovoltaic systems, subject to program loan limits and review.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Farmers Electric Cooperative member for the affected service location.
Install a permanently affixed conservation measure that qualifies under the cooperative's current grant rules.
Submit the cooperative's rebate and grant application with a description of the improvement, itemized receipts or invoices, and any requested installation documentation.
Remain within current per-application, annual, and available-funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The cooperative's current indexed grant page describes a fixed cost-share conservation grant rather than a scored competition. A timely, documented qualifying member project is likely to receive the stated support while annual funds and limits permit.
reviews.evidenceText: The current official page describes a member conservation grant with a percentage cost share, application requirements, and annual limits for permanently installed efficiency improvements. The full current form could not be retrieved.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Farmers Electric Cooperative member at the installation address.
Purchase and install equipment currently covered by the cooperative's rebate schedule and meet the applicable equipment and efficiency specifications.
Submit the current rebate and grant application with proof of purchase, equipment details, and installation documentation.
Comply with current customer, quantity, annual, and funding limits and permit verification when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The cooperative currently indexes fixed rebates for qualifying heat pumps, geothermal equipment, heat-pump water heaters, and related measures. Those claims are likely when documented and eligible, but the current official page was inaccessible and did not allow verification of the mapped lighting and refrigeration scope.
reviews.evidenceText: The current official rebate page identifies member equipment rebates and a common rebate and grant application. Search-accessible content supports heat-pump, geothermal, and heat-pump-water-heater offers, while complete current terms were not retrievable.

approvalRequirements: Be a Farmers RECC residential member at an eligible installation location.
Replace qualifying primary electric-resistance heating, or satisfy the separate new-manufactured-home provisions, with an eligible heat-pump system.
Install equipment meeting the current program and federal efficiency specifications.
Submit the rebate request with equipment and installation documentation and allow Farmers RECC to inspect or verify the completed installation.
Remain within the program's location and lifetime incentive limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The tariff provides fixed heat-pump incentives under objective member, replacement, equipment, and inspection conditions. A compliant heat-pump installation is likely to be approved, but the mapped furnace-retrofit category is not a qualifying stand-alone measure under this heat-pump program.
reviews.evidenceText: Farmers RECC's official program and tariff cover qualifying heat-pump replacements for residential members, set efficiency and location rules, and authorize inspection before the fixed rebate is paid. The program does not document a furnace-only rebate.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Firelands Electric Cooperative member for the applicable residential service.
Purchase and install a product or measure covered by the current member-program schedule before its stated program deadline.
Meet the measure-specific product, efficiency, contractor, testing, load-management, or installation rules.
Submit the required application with itemized receipts, product or contractor documentation, photographs or test results where applicable, and account information.
Complete any required on-site inspection or verification and apply while limited first-come program funds remain.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Firelands publishes fixed member rebates through June 30, 2027 for qualifying appliances, weatherization, heat pumps, thermostats, and electric-vehicle charging. These are administrative claims rather than competitive awards, but payment remains subject to measure rules, inspection, and limited funds.
reviews.evidenceText: The current member-program page extends the listed rebates through June 30, 2027. The official program guide specifies receipts, qualifying products, contractor or test documentation, inspections for selected measures, bill-credit payment, and limited first-come funding.

approvalRequirements: Offer or register renewable energy certificates produced by an eligible renewable generating resource rather than by a general efficiency retrofit.
Meet the applicable certificate registry, resource, geography, vintage, quantity, ownership, and environmental-attribute requirements for the active procurement or residential REC pathway.
Submit the required procurement response, registration, certifications, and pricing or transfer documentation by the applicable deadline.
Receive FirstEnergy acceptance and transfer verified certificates under the resulting purchase or program terms.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current official page concerns purchases of certified renewable energy credits from qualifying renewable generation. A window replacement does not generate a REC and therefore does not match the active award mechanism represented by the mapped retrofit.
reviews.evidenceText: FirstEnergy's current Ohio procurement page links renewable-energy-certificate purchase programs and prior REC solicitations. It does not offer an efficiency rebate or a certificate pathway for window replacements.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying nonresidential customer of Met-Ed, Penelec, Penn Power, or West Penn Power at the project site.
Use an eligible prescriptive, custom, retro-commissioning, or other current business-program pathway and satisfy its technical and savings requirements.

Submit the project application with a recent utility bill, W-9, itemized proposal, equipment specifications, cost information, and savings documentation before commitment when the selected pathway requires authorization.
Complete the approved scope and submit final invoices, the offer or approval documents, customer attestations, and final savings information.
Permit pre-project or post-project site review and final verification when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Pennsylvania business program offers prescriptive and calculated incentives under defined customer, technical, application, and completion rules. A qualifying project is likely to receive payment after final review, although the exact mapped CHP and study pathways must follow their applicable current program rules.
reviews.evidenceText: The current FirstEnergy Pennsylvania business site covers lighting, HVAC, motors and drives, refrigeration, custom projects, and retro-commissioning. Applications require customer, tax, quote, specification, and savings records, followed by final invoices and possible inspection before payment.

approvalRequirements: Maintain an eligible Met-Ed, Penelec, Penn Power, or West Penn Power residential account at the property.
Use the applicable current pathway, such as a utility home energy audit, qualifying appliance or HVAC offer, or approved envelope improvement.
Meet the current product, contractor, audit, efficiency, installation, and customer requirements for the selected measure.
Submit the rebate-portal or contractor documentation, including account information, invoices, product data, audit findings, and other requested proof.
Permit installation or post-work verification and apply while the applicable program remains funded.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current official materials substantiate no-cost home audits and envelope incentives, but the linked appliance and HVAC portal did not expose complete current measure-level terms for the broad legacy mapping. Awards are plausible for current qualifying measures, but the entire listed scope cannot be rated as likely from accessible evidence.
reviews.evidenceText: FirstEnergy currently offers Pennsylvania residential audits, reports, direct-install products, and rebates for eligible air sealing, duct sealing, and insulation. Complete current appliance and HVAC claim rules were not retrievable through the linked portal.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Potomac Edison Maryland commercial or industrial customer at the project site.
Select a currently qualifying lighting, HVAC, controls, variable-frequency-drive, custom, or other business measure and meet its technical specifications.
Obtain program preapproval before purchasing equipment or beginning installation.
Submit the application with a utility bill, W-9, itemized estimate, equipment specifications, and required qualified-product documentation.
After completion, submit final invoices, final equipment information, customer attestation, and any requested inspection or verification records.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Potomac Edison's current Maryland business incentives use mandatory preapproval and objective customer, equipment, and final-documentation criteria rather than competitive scoring. A fully approved and completed qualifying project is likely to be paid from reserved funds.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Potomac Edison business site lists lighting, HVAC, controls, and variable-frequency-drive incentives. It requires preapproval before purchase or installation and final invoices, specifications, attestations, and possible verification after completion.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Potomac Edison Maryland residential customer for the installation address.
Purchase a currently qualifying product or complete a qualifying improvement through a participating retailer, HVAC contractor, or Home Performance contractor as required by the selected offer.
Meet current product-list, efficiency, sizing, installation, and customer requirements and provide the account information needed for eligibility validation.
For Home Performance measures, complete the required assessment and contractor scope and satisfy any final testing or verification conditions.
Remain within current incentive limits and available program funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Most current Potomac Edison residential HVAC and appliance incentives are delivered as instant discounts through participating channels rather than competitively awarded. A qualifying customer and product are likely to receive the discount, although furnace eligibility may depend on a partner gas-utility pathway and individual appliance offers remain product-specific.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Maryland residential site provides instant discounts through participating retailers and contractors for qualifying heat pumps, geothermal systems, heat-pump water heaters, smart thermostats, and other products, with a separate assessment-based Home Performance pathway.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Flathead Electric Cooperative commercial customer at the project location.
Propose a currently qualifying business lighting, HVAC, or other efficiency project and meet the cooperative's technical requirements.
Contact the cooperative or submit the current commercial incentive materials before purchase or installation where advance project review is required.
Provide project, equipment, contractor, cost, and expected-savings information and, after completion, final invoices and installation documentation.
Allow any required site inspection or savings verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Flathead Electric currently indexes commercial efficiency incentives, including lighting opportunities, under a defined utility review process. A qualifying documented project is likely to receive an incentive, but the detailed official terms were blocked from retrieval.
reviews.evidenceText: The current official commercial rebate page identifies business energy-efficiency opportunities, including lighting. Detailed current application, preapproval, and HVAC requirements could not be retrieved because the official site blocked automated access.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Flathead Electric Cooperative residential member at the installation address.
Purchase and install a product or measure currently covered by the residential rebate program and meet its efficiency, equipment, contractor, and installation specifications.
Submit the measure-specific rebate application with proof of purchase, model or certification data, contractor bid or invoice, and other required documentation.
Obtain advance approval, inspection, or financing authorization where the selected measure requires it and complete any final verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Flathead Electric currently indexes residential rebates for heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, smart thermostats, windows, and efficient laundry equipment. These appear to be prescriptive member offers, so a compliant claim is likely, although the official pages blocked full review of every mapped measure and timing rule.
reviews.evidenceText: Flathead Electric's current official index and measure pages identify residential rebates for heat pumps, heat-pump water heaters, smart thermostats, windows, and other measures. Full application details were inaccessible from the official site.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Florida Keys Electric Cooperative residential member at the improved property.
Install a measure appearing on the current residential rebate list and satisfy its equipment, material, installation, and customer requirements.
Submit the rebate application with receipts or invoices, product and installation information, and any requested photographs or contractor records.
Remain within the current member and calendar-year incentive caps and permit verification when requested.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: FKEC's current indexed residential program describes fixed member rebates for qualifying envelope and efficiency measures rather than a competitive selection process. A current qualifying claim is likely, but detailed official terms for all mapped HVAC, roof, electric-vehicle, and audit categories were inaccessible.
reviews.evidenceText: The current official residential rebate page indexes incentives for measures including window film or solar screens, insulation, weatherization, and room air conditioning, with member and annual limits. Complete current rules for every mapped measure could not be retrieved.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Florida Keys Electric Cooperative member with the required billing or account history.
Propose a qualifying solar photovoltaic or battery-storage installation by an eligible vendor and provide the project proposal and cost documentation.
Submit the solar-loan application with account, property, project, contractor, and financial information requested by the cooperative.
Pass member, project, account, and credit or repayment review and satisfy interconnection, permit, insurance, and security requirements.
Execute the loan documents and complete the approved installation and final inspection before final disbursement or account treatment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: FKEC currently offers loans for qualifying solar and battery projects, but financing depends on account history, project and contractor qualification, underwriting, and completion conditions. Retrofit eligibility alone does not assure loan approval.
reviews.evidenceText: The current official solar-loan materials describe financing for solar and battery storage installed by qualified vendors and require a member application and account history. The full manual and underwriting details were not retrievable.

approvalRequirements: Own an eligible property in a Florida jurisdiction that has authorized the applicable PACE program.
Be current on property taxes and mortgage obligations and satisfy the program's delinquency, default, lien, equity, and property-eligibility rules.
Propose an improvement that is confirmed as eligible by the local PACE program and use an approved contractor.
Submit the application and supporting property, ownership, mortgage, project, and cost documents and complete the property-based financing review.
Execute the assessment agreement, obtain permits, complete the work, and pass final inspection or signoff before contractor payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current Florida PACE materials establish property, county, contractor, and financing review requirements, but the official pages reviewed did not verify battery storage as an eligible improvement. Award likelihood for the mapped battery project cannot be established without local program-specific evidence.
reviews.evidenceText: Florida PACE currently requires an authorizing local jurisdiction, current tax and mortgage status, property and lien review, an approved contractor, permits, and final completion confirmation. Current official eligibility evidence for battery storage was not found.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible FPL business customer at the project location.
Use a current prescriptive lighting or HVAC offer, or propose a custom project meeting the program's minimum summer-demand reduction and cost-effectiveness requirements.
Provide project, equipment, cost, operating, and savings information required for program screening.
Obtain FPL approval before proceeding with a custom-incentive project.
Complete the approved work and provide final invoices, equipment records, and access for verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: FPL currently supports business lighting and HVAC offers and a preapproved custom-incentive pathway, but the current official pages reviewed did not directly substantiate the mapped refrigeration and submetering measures. A qualifying current project can be funded, but the full legacy mapping is only partially supported.
reviews.evidenceText: FPL's current business site lists lighting and HVAC programs. The custom program requires a qualifying demand reduction, cost-effectiveness, project information, and FPL approval before implementation; direct current rebate evidence for refrigeration and submetering was not found.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible FPL residential customer at the installation property.
Use an FPL-approved Participating Independent Contractor for the qualifying central air-conditioning replacement or ceiling-insulation work.
For air conditioning, install a qualifying complete indoor-and-outdoor system meeting the current minimum efficiency requirements.
For insulation, satisfy the current attic-access and existing-insulation-level requirements and install the qualifying scope.
Allow the contractor and FPL to validate account, equipment, site, and completion eligibility for the instant invoice credit.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: FPL's current air-conditioning and ceiling-insulation incentives are fixed instant credits applied by approved contractors. An eligible customer receiving a qualifying installation should ordinarily receive the credit without a competitive award decision.
reviews.evidenceText: FPL currently provides instant residential credits through approved contractors for qualifying complete air-conditioning systems and attic insulation that meets the published efficiency and site conditions.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Florida Public Utilities commercial electric customer and, where required, the property owner for the installation site.
Purchase and install a currently qualifying commercial electric measure and meet the published equipment, efficiency, ducting, service-area, and installation rules.
Submit the signed rebate application within the current filing period with account information, equipment data, proof of purchase, and installation documentation.
Permit FPU to verify customer, equipment, and installation eligibility and remain within current program limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: FPU's current commercial electric page supports objective lighting, HVAC or heat-pump, and chiller rebates, so qualifying claims can be approved. The page did not substantiate the mapped window-replacement and window-film categories, making the broad legacy opportunity only partially supported.
reviews.evidenceText: The current commercial electric rebate page lists lighting and qualifying HVAC or heat-pump incentives and requires a signed application within one year with customer and equipment documentation. Current window and window-film rebates were not shown.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Florida Public Utilities residential electric customer and satisfy any property-ownership requirement for the installation address.
Install a qualifying ducted high-efficiency heat pump or air-conditioning system meeting the current minimum efficiency specifications.
Submit the signed rebate application within the current filing period with account information, proof of purchase, equipment ratings, and installation records.
Permit verification of the customer, equipment, installation, and service-area requirements.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: FPU currently offers an objective residential HVAC rebate for qualifying systems, but the current official page reviewed did not substantiate an efficient-pump replacement incentive. Approval is plausible for the supported HVAC measures, not for the full mapped scope.
reviews.evidenceText: The current residential electric page provides rebates for qualifying ducted heat pumps and air-conditioning systems and requires a signed application within one year. A current efficient-pump rebate was not shown.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Florida Public Utilities commercial natural-gas customer or qualifying program participant at the installation address.
Purchase and install new qualifying commercial-grade natural-gas equipment covered by the current rebate schedule.
Submit the rebate claim within the current filing period with account, equipment, purchase, and installation information.
Comply with current equipment-condition, fuel-conversion or replacement, quantity, per-appliance, and annual customer limits.
Permit FPU to verify the installation and claim before payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current FPU commercial gas program clearly supports qualifying high-efficiency fryers and other listed gas appliances through an administrative rebate claim. The current page did not substantiate the mapped general high-efficiency HVAC category, so the full opportunity scope is only partly evidenced.
reviews.evidenceText: FPU currently lists commercial natural-gas appliance rebates, including efficient fryers, and requires new qualifying equipment, timely filing, and compliance with per-appliance and annual limits. A general commercial HVAC rebate was not verified.

approvalRequirements: Be an eligible Florida Public Utilities residential natural-gas customer at the installation address.
Purchase and install a new qualifying natural-gas furnace under the current replacement or fuel-conversion category.
Submit the online or signed rebate claim within one year with account information, equipment details, proof of purchase, and installation documentation.
Meet current product, installation, customer, and quantity rules and permit claim verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: FPU publishes fixed residential natural-gas furnace rebates under objective customer, equipment, installation, and filing rules. A complete qualifying claim is likely to be paid after administrative verification.
reviews.evidenceText: The current residential gas rebate page lists qualifying furnace replacement and conversion rebates and directs customers to file through the rebate center within one year of purchase or installation.

approvalRequirements: Be a qualifying Silicon Valley Power nonresidential customer at the Santa Clara installation site.
Select new food-service, refrigeration, or demand-controlled kitchen-ventilation equipment appearing in the current qualifying program materials and meet its technical specifications.
Submit the application, equipment specifications, project cost, and other required technical information and obtain written Silicon Valley Power preapproval before purchase or installation.
Complete the approved installation within the authorization period and request any required post-installation inspection.
Submit final invoices and completion documentation within the stated deadlines and remain within measure, customer, and program funding limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current Food Service Equipment Rebate Program uses fixed incentives for qualifying refrigeration and kitchen-ventilation equipment after written preapproval and final verification. Those supported measures are likely after approval, but the mapped battery-storage and low-flow-fixture categories are not part of the current food-service application, so the opportunity as mapped is only partially awardable.
reviews.evidenceText: Silicon Valley Power's current program covers qualifying ENERGY STAR commercial refrigeration and demand-controlled kitchen ventilation, requires written preapproval before installation, and requires completion, inspection, invoices, and specifications on stated timelines. Battery storage and low-flow fixtures are not listed in this food-service application.
